t: 2808. Minimum Seconds to Equalize a Circular Array
o: Each second, information spreads one step in each direction on a circle. If we settle on value v, every cell becomes v within ⌈gap/2⌉ seconds, where gap is the largest clockwise distance between consecutive occurrences of v (including the wrap-around gap). Why half? A value spreads outward from both neighboring occurrences simultaneously, meeting in the middle of the largest gap. In Example 2, value 3 occurs at indices 2,3 with wrap gap from 3 to 2 of length 3 (via 4,0,1), giving ⌈3/2⌉=2. Try every distinct value and take the minimum.
k: A value propagates 1 step/second in both directions; the bottleneck is the largest arc with no occurrence of that value.

a.i: Record indices of each value. For value v with sorted occurrence indices, the gaps are consecutive differences and the wrap-around gap (first + n − last). The time needed is max_gap // 2; minimize across values.
s: Build a map value → list of indices.
For each value, compute the maximum of consecutive index differences and the wrap gap; take half (integer division).
Return the minimum over all values.
a.t: O(n) — each index is visited once while building lists and once while scanning gaps

w: Don't forget the circular wrap-around gap (idx[0] + n − idx[last]). Integer division by 2 is correct because spread is simultaneous from both sides of a gap. Edge cases: all elements equal → 0; a value occurring once has a single wrap gap of n. Follow-up: what if replacement were asynchronous (sequential)? The dynamics change completely.
